items.item: An object store is a flat key-to-blob namespace with no filesystem underneath; a prefix is a shared leading substring, not a directory

at.step: A flat namespace, not a filesystem

items.item: Writes are whole-object: PUT replaces the whole object, and a general-purpose bucket has no append and no rename, only COPY then DELETE

at.step: A flat namespace, not a filesystem

items.item: Strong read-after-write consistency (since December 2020 on S3) means the next read sees a successful write, and a racing read never returns a torn object

at.step: Strong read-after-write, since 2020

items.item: What strong consistency still does not give: a cross-key transaction, so swapping or atomically creating several objects together is not possible

at.step: Strong read-after-write, since 2020

items.item: A request's cost is alpha plus bytes over beta, with alpha in the tens to hundreds of milliseconds; this is the T(n) model at its most latency-dominated extreme

at.step: The cost of one request: α + n/β

items.item: Because request latency is a distribution, a job that waits on many requests is bounded by a high percentile (p99 or worse), not the median

at.step: The cost of one request: α + n/β

items.item: The break-even range size is alpha times beta; below it a request is latency-bound, above it bandwidth-bound, which is why cloud vendors recommend multi-megabyte ranges

at.step: Predict: where does waiting equal transferring?

items.item: Throughput on object storage comes from concurrency, not from any single fast request, and there is no per-bucket bandwidth cap

at.step: Predict: how many requests fill the link?

items.item: Each prefix has its own request-rate ceiling; exceeding it returns 503 Slow Down as back-pressure, and the fix is spreading keys across more prefixes, not retrying forever on one

at.step: Each prefix has its own ceiling

items.item: A Range GET reads a contiguous slice of an object; combined with a columnar footer at the end of the file, a query can fetch only the column chunks it needs

at.step: A range GET reads just a slice

items.item: Multipart upload makes large-object writes resumable per part and keeps the object invisible to readers until the final assembly call succeeds, preserving whole-object atomicity

at.step: Large objects upload in parts

items.item: Conditional writes (If-None-Match / If-Match) are a compare-and-set primitive that, combined with strong consistency, lets a table format commit without an external lock service

at.step: Predict: two writers, one key

items.item: S3 Express One Zone directory buckets are the one exception to the whole-object, no-append, no-rename model, trading availability-zone scope for append and atomic rename

at.out: A named exception the reel does not animate; covered in index.mdx's deep dive, not central to the general-purpose contract this topic teaches.
